text:
Donald Knuth is a computer scientist and writer renowned for his work in mathematics and computer science. He began his early studies in physics at the Case Institute of Technology before switching to mathematics. At Caltech, he received his PhD in mathematics. Knuth established his field of study as "Analysis of algorithms" and became a founding editor of the Case Institute's Engineering and Science Review.
He is best known for his monumental series, *The Art of Computer Programming* ( *TAOCP* ), which he outlined as needing seven volumes to thoroughly cover the subject. His work also includes the creation of the TeX typesetting system and Metafont. Furthermore, he developed the concept of literate programming, where programmers write programs as works of literature, embodied in the WEB system. Knuth has received numerous high honors, including the Turing Award, the National Science Foundation Fellowship, and the National Academy of Sciences election.
